extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists and professionals in astronomy, geology, hygiene, public health, and related disciplines
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying evaluative standards and methodological recommendations embedded in a multidisciplinary Nature issue (astronomy, geology, hygiene, public health). Emphasises how to judge data, sampling, statistics, and recommended procedures reported in short communications and meeting summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of correlation ratio in astronomical statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Should not the correlation ratio be used in preference to the coefficient of correlation? The former expresses the degree of approximation to a smooth curve, the latter the approximation to a straight line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale given: astronomical regression curves are rarely straight lines and the variable ranges are large, so the correlation ratio better captures approximation to a smooth curve. Recommendation: in all treatment of astronomical statistics use the correlation ratio rather than simple correlation coefficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of specialised/selected material (sample bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cape Photo- graphic Durchmusterung revision concentrated upon a particular class of stars near the limit of the C.P.D., which had escaped registration owing to some abnormality, generally redness. This specially selected material has been further specialised... This is the material from which Prof. Pearson and Miss Gibson extract their conclusions about the stars in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: conclusions about a general population should not be drawn from material that was selected for specific abnormalities (photographic defects, variability, large proper motion, redness, faintness). Ensure representativeness of sample before generalising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meteor observation reporting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting meteor observations include precise local time/date, estimated magnitude, observed path with start and end coordinates, streak length, radiant position, and observing conditions (e.g., clouding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Denning reported 'On September 27 at 9h. 54m. I saw a very swift meteor of about 1½ mag. ... leaving a streak of about 10°' and gave start/end bearings and computed radiant; also compared behaviour to known showers (Leonids) and reported frequency and historical records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay full publication until identifications and investigations complete (geological reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fuller particulars reserved until the fossils have been exactly identified and the investigation completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If stratigraphical claims (e.g., discovery of marly, lignitiferous, glauconitic limestone of Upper Eocene/Oligocene age) are preliminary, withhold complete description until fossils and investigation are confirmed; report only tentative notice until verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid basing prophylaxis on unstable 'types' of pathogens
rubrics_metrics.description: There would be real danger, from the medical as well as the hygienic point of view, in making such unstable differences a basis for laying down principles for the prophylaxis of tuberculosis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prof. Arloing argued that described 'types' of tubercle bacillus are often imperfectly defined and blended; variability can explain observed differences. Public-health policy and prophylaxis should not be founded on transient or poorly defined microbial types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider inhalation primary route for tuberculosis in adults; alimentary (milk) route important in children
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments and autopsy evidence indicate inhalation as the chief mode of infection in man (via droplets); alimentary tract infection (notably from milk of tuberculous cows) is especially frequent in children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple speakers summarised evidence: inhalation requires far fewer bacilli to infect than alimentary route; public-health measures should prioritise controlling airborne expectoration but also address milk safety for children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typhoid organism isolation/differentiation method
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification, isolation and differentiation of causative micro-organisms of typhoid/paratyphoid using sugar nutrient media containing a small percentage of the anilin dye malachite green.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As presented by Prof. Löffler: use of specific nutrient media with malachite green assists in isolation and differentiation of typhoid-related organisms; methodological recommendation for laboratory practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise mild or inapparent carriers in typhoid control
rubrics_metrics.description: Mild cases, sometimes amounting merely to slight indisposition, though the individual may be but little, if at all, ill, he at the same time excretes the bacillus, and thus may be a source of infection to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Epidemiological criterion: surveillance and control programs must account for asymptomatic or mild excreting individuals as important infection sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ship rat eradication by controlled gas exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred method to rid ships of rats: expose the hold to a mixed gas produced in a generator, consisting of 5% carbon monoxide, 18% carbon dioxide, and 77% nitrogen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dr. Giemsa advocated this specific gas composition as an effective practical method; inclusion as a procedural option for maritime plague control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider preventive inoculation (attenuated cultures) for plague prophylaxis
rubrics_metrics.description: Preventive inoculation using living but attenuated cultures of the plague bacillus is proposed as the mode of combating the disease which holds out the most likelihood of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dr. Strong argued for vaccination-style prophylaxis for plague; policy-level consideration and further evaluation suggested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research on insect vectors should clarify structure, development, and nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.description: There is present lack of knowledge concerning the structure and developmental history of ticks, and the confused nomenclature of these insects now existing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For insects-as-carriers studies, priority should be given to taxonomic clarification and life-history research before making definitive claims about vector roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dietetics recommendation: favour ample protein proportion pending better knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Besides albumen, fat, and carbohydrates, man requires certain substances related to nitrogenous ingredients of food. (2) Digestive ferments and internal secretions are nitrogenous and depend on albumen intake. (3) Until relations better understood, it will be advisable for general biological and hygienic reasons to favour an ample proportion of protein in practical nutrition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prof. Forster's three-point conclusion recommends erring on the side of higher protein in public/nutritional guidance until quantity/quality relations of proteins are clarified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupational/industrial disease mitigation: improve lighting, ventilation, and water supplies
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial diseases (lead and mercurial poisoning, those from dust, strain, etc.) and suggestions were made to mitigate these evils; lighting, ventilation and water supplies were also dealt with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public-health and workplace interventions should prioritise environmental controls such as improved lighting, ventilation and clean water to reduce industrial disease burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mining safety limits and pressure-change procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: No ill effects result with pressures below about three atmospheres, but above these, unless the pressure is increased or decreased step by step, grave effects may be produced. The optimum wet-bulb temperature is below 27°C; the maximum that can be sustained without danger being 31°C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Dr. Haldane's research: compressed-air work should respect pressure thresholds and require gradual pressurisation/depressurisation; maintain wet-bulb temperature below 27°C for safety, never above ~31°C without special measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serum therapy method for typhoid (production and reported effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grow the typhoid bacillus in a spleen broth medium for a week, heat to 55°C, and inject into horses; the serum of the latter acquires properties which usually act favourably on the course of the disease when injected into the patient. Reported mortality: general 17% vs 4.3% in 1,000 cases treated with this serum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prof. Chantemesse's protocol and outcome data are presented as evidence supporting serum treatment; method details (medium, duration, heating temp, animal host) are explicit and intended to guide replication/evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardisation of bacteriological methods for drinking-water
rubrics_metrics.description: An international commission should be formed to devise standard methods for the chemical and bacteriological examinations of drinking water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prof. Schattenfroh urged establishment of harmonised, standard protocols internationally for water testing to ensure comparable and reliable public-health assessments.
